description: The line plot illustrates the performance of various models in terms of AUC (Area Under the Curve) percentage as a function of the number of training samples, denoted by N, on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 20. The y-axis, labeled AUC (%), spans from 75 to 100, with major tick marks at intervals of 5. The x-axis, labeled N, is logarithmically scaled, with labeled tick marks at 1, 5, 10, and 20. The plot contains six distinct lines, each representing a different model configuration, identified by unique colors and markers: a blue line with circle markers, an orange line with square markers, a green line with star markers, a red line with diamond markers, a purple line with triangle markers, and a yellow line with inverted triangle markers. The blue line starts at an AUC of approximately 94% at N=1 and increases to about 100% at N=20. The orange line begins at around 87% and rises to approximately 100% at N=20. The green line starts at about 87% and increases to roughly 99% at N=20. The red line begins at approximately 88% and rises to about 99% at N=20. The purple line starts at around 81% at N=1, increases to about 83% at N=5, then sharply rises to approximately 100% at N=6, and remains at 100% for N=10 and N=20. The yellow line starts at about 85% and increases to approximately 100% at N=20.
